quiz.q: According to Professor V.R. Mehta, why did Western scholars often fail to recognize Indian political thought?
options: Western thinkers analyze concepts through rigid dichotomies, whereas Indian thought approaches ethics and politics as a continuity.
Western scholars believed ancient Indian texts focused purely on statecraft and completely ignored spiritual salvation.
Western traditions reject sovereign authority, whereas Indian thinkers subordinated all social institutions to royal command.
Western thinkers view history progressively, whereas Indian traditions completely denied the existence of moral duty.
quiz.why: Professor V.R. Mehta explained that while the West separates ethics from politics through dichotomies, Indian thought treats Dharma and Danda as an integrated continuum.

quiz.q: How do Dharmashastra and Dandashastra differ in their treatment of Dharma and Danda?
options: Dharmashastra rejects coercive state authority, while Dandashastra completely eliminates all moral obligations.
Their difference is of degree: Dharmashastra focuses primarily on Dharma, while Dandashastra prioritizes Dandaniti.
Dharmashastra applies only to ascetics, whereas Dandashastra regulates the duties of common citizens.
Their difference is absolute: Dharmashastra discusses cosmic law, whereas Dandashastra focuses exclusively on theology.
quiz.why: As noted by Bhikhu Parekh, both traditions contain both concepts, differing only in whether Dharma or Dandaniti forms the central focus.

quiz.q: In Manusmriti, what does the distinction between the king's divine personality and lack of divine rights signify?
options: The king possesses infallible absolute authority and cannot be judged or restrained by moral law.
The king holds temporary divine powers that transfer completely to Vedic priests during military conflicts.
The king rules with total personal discretion because Brahma granted him exemption from cosmic penalties.
The king derives authority from God but remains strictly subordinate to and accountable under Raj Dharma.
quiz.why: While the king embodies traits of various deities, he possesses no absolute divine rights and is strictly bound by Raj Dharma.

quiz.q: Why is the origin of the state in Manusmriti characterized as a quasi-contractual theory?
options: The social agreement was made directly between the ruler and the subjects without divine intervention.
The four varnas negotiated a power-sharing constitution to elect a king from among the Brahmins.
The covenant occurred between man and God, where people requested Brahma to create a king.
The king signed a formal legal charter granting unconditional rights to citizens to avoid anarchy.
quiz.why: It is considered quasi-contractual because the pact was between people and God, who created King Manu to deliver society from Matsyanyaya.
